clue.text: Belittle fine hair, reportedly grizzled

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the following word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: down is soft fine hair or feathers
grizzled hair has greyed

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a person whose fine hair has gone grey.
explanation.definitionFit: To downgrade someone is to lower their status or standing, which is a way of belittling them.

clue.text: Slowly speak of attraction, and pull at last

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: a draw is something that attracts crowds
the final letter of pull

explanation.surface: Describing a slow speaker's magnetic charm and pull.
explanation.definitionFit: To drawl is to talk in a slow, lazy manner with drawn-out vowels.

clue.text: Computer model of firearm we designed

indicators.note: something designed has been planned and put together, so these letters are assembled anew

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A digital mock-up of a gun we came up with ourselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A wireframe is a skeletal three-dimensional computer representation made only of lines and edges.

clue.text: Scot sawing a leg off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so these letters are spoiled into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scotsman is cutting through a limb, in gruesome fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sawing a leg off' reads naturally as one action; 'off' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Glaswegian is a native of Glasgow, the largest city in Scotland, so is a Scot.

clue.text: Start to adjust ball bearing very early

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept
bearing means carrying, so the word for the ball holds the next piece inside it

blocks.note: the first letter of adjust
a ball is a formal dance
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Setting up the ball bearings well ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ball bearing' is a machine part in the surface, but the words are split: a ball, then bearing as carrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Advance used as an adjective, as in advance notice, means done or arriving early, ahead of time.

clue.text: Completely timeless vamp is supremely powerful woman

indicators.note: without any time at all, so every T, the time symbol, is taken out

blocks.note: a vamp is a seductive woman

explanation.surface: An ageless femme fatale is a woman of great power.
explanation.walkthrough: T stands for time; both of the Ts in TEMPTRESS are removed.
explanation.definitionFit: An empress rules an empire, so she holds the highest rank of power among women.

clue.text: Liberal dons prosper and flourish

indicators.note: to don is to put on clothing, so the second word wears the first like a garment

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
a business that booms prospers

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician dresses up, thrives and does well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like university teachers, but here it is the verb meaning puts on.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant in bloom is flowering, and to bloom also means to thrive or prosper generally.

clue.text: Asked criminal to cover me, heading off

indicators.note: in a down clue, covering means sitting on top, so this word goes above the next one
with its head removed, a word loses its opening letter and keeps the rest

blocks.note: bad as in wicked or unlawful
me without its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone requested that a crook give them an alibi.
explanation.definitionFit: Bade is a past tense of bid, which can mean to ask or command someone to do something.

clue.text: Complies with order, knocking stuffing out of yobs

indicators.note: the stuffing is the filling, so the inside is removed and only the outside letters remain

blocks.note: OBE is the Order of the British Empire
the outside letters of yobs

explanation.surface: Someone follows instructions to give thugs a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: Yobs is British slang for loutish young men.
explanation.definitionFit: To obey is to do as instructed, which is what complying with a rule or order involves.

clue.text: Badly manage squeamish and lethargic nurses

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold something close, so these words cradle the answer within them

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning these words

explanation.surface: A queasy and sluggish carer makes a poor job of the ward.
explanation.definitionFit: To mishandle a situation is to deal with it incompetently or clumsily.

clue.text: Vessel of canoers that oddly disappeared

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions vanish, leaving only the second, fourth and so on

blocks.note: the even-placed letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A boat used by canoeists has strangely vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a canoe, which the surface encourages, but it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery leaving the heart, and arteries are blood vessels.

clue.text: Vacuity of Victor, annoying in spades

indicators.note: annoying means disturbing, so the following letters are stirred up into a new order

blocks.note: Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Victor is irritating in large measure, and empty-headed with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In spades' reads as an idiom meaning abundantly, but it is just the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Vapidness is dullness and lack of substance or ideas, the same emptiness as vacuity.

clue.text: Radical female sib enthralled by French painter

indicators.note: someone enthralled is held captive, so these words sit inside the next one

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
a twin is a sibling
Fernand Léger, the French cubist painter

explanation.surface: An extremist sister falls under the spell of a French artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A left-winger holds strongly socialist or progressive views, and a radical is someone with extreme political opinions.

clue.text: Bones huge as boomerangs

indicators.note: a boomerang flies back the way it came, so the word before it returns in the opposite direction

blocks.note: OS stands for outsize
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bones as big as boomerangs, perhaps from some prehistoric creature.
explanation.walkthrough: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is the Latin plural of os, used in anatomy for bones.

clue.text: Stuffed admiral in hold

blocks.note: someone stuffed after a meal is full
Horatio Nelson, the British naval hero

explanation.surface: A taxidermy figure of a naval commander is kept in a ship's store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffed admiral' suggests a museum exhibit and 'hold' a ship's cargo space; hold is the wrestling sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A full nelson is a wrestling grip in which both arms are locked behind the opponent's neck.

clue.text: Argue with Republican point of view

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
R is the abbreviation for Republican
an angle is a viewpoint or perspective

explanation.surface: Disagreeing with a Republican's political perspective.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrangle is to have a long, noisy dispute, which means to argue or quarrel.

clue.text: Timid setters have to entertain a couple of kings

indicators.note: entertaining is holding guests inside, so the phrase takes the next pieces into its middle

blocks.note: setters referring to themselves
have to means need to
taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king, twice

explanation.surface: Crossword compilers must host two monarchs, a nerve-racking prospect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setters' read as a single entertainer misleads: it is the setters' own 'we', and the pair of words 'have to' together form the host that opens up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being weak-kneed means lacking courage or resolve, so timid and easily scared.

clue.text: Virile chap, explosive and well practised

blocks.note: a stud is a sexually virile man
IED is an improvised explosive device

explanation.surface: A macho man with a bomb who has rehearsed his act carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: A studied manner or performance is deliberately rehearsed and polished rather than spontaneous.

clue.text: Lover wearing scent picked up at counter

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting something up turns it to read from the bottom upwards
counter means contrary, so these two letters run the opposite way

blocks.note: someone wearing a coat is in it
an aroma is a scent
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sweetheart in perfume is noticed at the shop counter.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a female lover or sweetheart, from the Italian for one who is in love.

clue.text: President pursued by fat lover

indicators.note: something pursued has another thing coming after it, so the next piece follows the first

blocks.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US president
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A head of state is chased by a heavyweight romantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Abelard, the medieval French philosopher, is famous for his tragic love affair with Héloïse.

clue.text: Sweetie left in bottle

indicators.note: in places one thing within the other

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
bottle is British slang for courage or nerve

explanation.surface: A sweet was left behind inside a jar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' looks like a container, but it is the British slang sense of nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Darling and sweetie are both affectionate terms of address for a loved one.

clue.text: United relegated from league after midfielder's first international benefit

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word it belongs to
a team relegated is sent out of its division, so that letter is removed from the word
after places the shortened word behind the pieces that come before it

blocks.note: the first letter of midfielder
I is the abbreviation for international
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football team sent down from its league after its star midfielder made an international appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: The U is taken out of LEAGUE to leave LEAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mileage is figurative advantage or use got out of something, as in getting political mileage from it.

clue.text: Recalling one's bet is bad move

indicators.note: recalling calls something back, so the contraction runs in the opposite direction

blocks.note: one's read as one is, for the speaker I am, shortened
a stake is a wager

explanation.surface: Taking back a wager is an unwise choice.
explanation.walkthrough: From the setter's viewpoint, one's means I'm.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake is an error or wrong decision, which is what a bad move in a game or life amounts to.

clue.text: Heartily necking beer and cabbage

indicators.note: taken from the heart, meaning the central letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: the middle letter of necking
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Enthusiastically downing a pint, followed by a plate of greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Necking' is British slang for drinking quickly, which makes the surface convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: Kale is a leafy green vegetable belonging to the cabbage family.

clue.text: Can probably empty potty

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its contents, leaving only the outside letters

blocks.note: can is slang for a toilet, as is loo
the outer letters of probably

explanation.surface: A toilet probably needs emptying, potty training in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word is misleading: 'Can' and 'potty' look like toilets, but potty is the definition, meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Potty is British informal for mad or slightly crazy, and loopy is a similar casual term.

clue.text: Fed up of bad serfs running amok

indicators.note: running amok means rampaging wildly, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lord who is tired of his unruly peasants rioting.
explanation.walkthrough: Brassed off is British slang for annoyed or fed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being brassed off is the informal British way of saying you are thoroughly annoyed and weary of something.

clue.text: Thick journalist is doomed

blocks.note: thick in the sense of wide or bulky
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A dim reporter has no future.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fated has its outcome determined by destiny, usually an unhappy one, so it is doomed.

clue.text: Observed articulate contretemps

indicators.note: to articulate is to utter clearly, so the word is judged by its spoken form

blocks.note: making a scene is having a public row

explanation.surface: Someone noticed an eloquent disagreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulate' looks like an adjective describing the dispute, but it is the verb meaning to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen is the past participle of see, meaning watched or noticed, just as observed is.

clue.text: Secrets of earl and girl behind boozer

indicators.note: behind puts the word before it after the word that comes next

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for earl
a sot is a drunkard
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A nobleman and a young woman share secrets at the back of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' is British slang both for a pub and a heavy drinker; here it is the drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoterica are obscure matters understood only by a few insiders, so they are like closely kept secrets.

clue.text: Limited name-dropping is entertaining

indicators.note: entertaining guests means having them inside, so the first piece is held within the second

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
scat is an animal's dropping

explanation.surface: Showing off famous acquaintances is a bit of fun, but only to a point.
explanation.walkthrough: Ignore the hyphen: 'name-dropping' is not boasting but two pieces, the name and the dropping.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely sufficient or meagre in amount, hence limited.

clue.text: Fulfil desire to be master

blocks.note: to do a task is to carry it out
a yen is a longing

explanation.surface: An ambition to become the boss and have it granted.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the most senior or respected person in a field, an acknowledged master of it.

clue.text: New Englander in Danish territory

indicators.note: new means freshly made, so the following letters are formed into something different

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone from New England finds themselves in a Danish possession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Englander' looks like a single phrase for an American from New England; 'New' is split off as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenland is a vast Arctic island that is an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.
